dedupe_keys.name: techno economic analysis framework for leo satellite direct to device services global non terrestrial network

description: This paper presents a techno-economic analysis framework for LEO satellite direct-to-device (D2D) services that link unmodified 3GPP handsets to space-based broadband. The framework combines a global satellite constellation model, radio propagation with ITU-R compliant atmospheric and rainfall attenuation, 3GPP-compliant capacity calculations, realistic global population data and a cost model for capital and operating expenses of space and ground segments, and compares three architectural options for a global non-terrestrial network. Its economic assessment finds that D2D services can be provided at a monthly cost per subscriber comparable to terrestrial services with a positive return on investment, and points to Open RAN as a route to cost-effective satellite D2D. Producer: Aijaz, Li and Gufran; first submitted on 6 October 2025 (eight pages, 13 figures) and accepted for presentation at IEEE/IFIP WMNC 2025. Coverage: global. Access: free PDF and HTML on arXiv; the framework is described as implemented through significant enhancements to an open-source tool, with an emphasis on reproducibility, but the tool was not named on the abstract page. Licence and cost: free to read; the code licence is not confirmed, and the paper is under the CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. Caveats: results rest on assumed cost and demand parameters, and the paper was not read beyond the abstract page. Simulation uses: it supports capacity planning and investment appraisal of direct-to-device coverage extension. Related records: the NIST O-RAN module for ns-3 (model-nist-ns3-oran) and the Universal Techno-Economic Model (model-utem-universal-techno-economic-model).
